results.gate: 5 S = 0 at the centre; off-centre S matches the exact spherical form
results.detail:
exact octahedral configuration, |S| at the centre: 5.910e-17 (round-off)
K there equals exp(s_0) I to 4.4e-16 -- an isotropic rescaling, no preferred direction
random ball, |S_rr| at the centre 4.32e-04 against Monte-Carlo noise 7.1e-04
largest |MC - exact quadrature| over all probe radii: 7.94e-04 (1.1 sigma_MC)
OFF-CENTRE S IS NOT ZERO AND MUST NOT BE: at 1200 kpc inside the ball S_rr = +0.0171, at 2500 kpc outside it +0.5151.
Reading 'S -> 0 for a spherical distribution' as a statement about every
point is wrong -- the direction field n_a(x) seen from an off-centre point
is not isotropic.  What symmetry requires is the form lambda(r)(rhat rhat
- I/3), and the largest residual from that form, over the probes where |S|
rises above the Monte-Carlo floor, is 0.0436.

largest 64->96 change: 1.471%  (threshold 2%)
self-convergence order at 500/1000/1414 kpc: 1.25 2.05 -0.93
The curve is NOT flat, which is what it has to be: a flat error
curve versus resolution would mean a modelling mismatch rather
than a discretisation error.  Convergence is first-to-second
order rather than clean second order because the tensor field K
itself varies on the scale of the individual members, which the
grid only marginally resolves -- see the resolution_check block
of mechanism_map.json, where the same question is asked of k
directly at the amplitudes the map actually uses.

largest 4 Mpc -> 8 Mpc change: 0.357%  (threshold 2%)
The Dirichlet shell comes from the spherical reduction of the
same equation with the model's own k(r), so the far field is
consistent with the interior rather than imposed as Newtonian.

results.gate: A4 sign convention fixed by measurement, not by intuition
results.detail:
uniform-K anchor reproduces sqrt(k_par/k_perp) to 1.52%
K = exp[-alpha C], alpha > 0 (the brief's sign): the response along
  the channel relative to across it is 0.9914 < 1 -- gravity is WEAKER
  along the line joining the wells and stronger transverse to it.
K = exp[+alpha C]: 1.0072 > 1 -- this is the sign that makes the
  response STRONGER ALONG THE CHANNELS.
Both are implemented as sign=-1 and sign=+1 and both are scanned in
the mechanism map.  The naive argument (a poorer conductor needs a
larger gradient) is wrong here because flux can be diverted; it is
right only where no diversion is possible, i.e. for a radially aligned
K in spherical symmetry, which is the regime the shell-averaged
boost lives in.

results.gate: A5 1-D surrogate reproduces the 3-D solve to a stated accuracy
results.detail:
largest 3D/1D departure, harmonic mean:   5.81%
largest 3D/1D departure, arithmetic mean: 15.15%
The surrogate always UNDER-predicts the boost, so the amplitudes the
map reports are upper limits on what is needed, and the galaxy damage
it reports is an over-estimate.  The headline points are re-run in
full 3-D anyway (headline_3d in mechanism_map.json), where the map
is reproduced to ~2%.
